g.text: "description": "Name for a new suite. Required (non-empty) when no `suiteId` is given."
"description": "Inline test cases to upsert into the suite before running.",
"description": "Servers (by ID) the run connects to. Required when creating a new suite; optional on reruns \u2014 when omit
ted, the run connects the suite's saved server selection (the set its snapshot references). A rerun of a suite with no saved selec
tion is rejected with `VALIDATION_ERROR` (`details.reason: \"NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION\"`). Rejected outright for a suite with att
ached environments (`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE\"`): the environment supplies a closed set that a serve
r override cannot change, so accepting one would connect a different set than the run is stamped with.",
"description": "When true, skip per-case upsert and rerun the persisted suite. A bare `suiteId` with no `tests` is always tr
"description": "Optional per-provider model API keys (e.g. `{ \"anthropic\": \"sk-ant-\u2026\" }`). Falls back to your organ
"description": "The floor a run must clear, as a PERCENT in [0, 100] \u2014 80 means 80%. `minimumPassRatePercent` is the ca
nonical spelling (the unit is in the name); `minimumPassRate` is the deprecated alias for it. Send exactly one. THE NAME DISAMBIGU
ATES THE UNIT: a value in (0, 1) is accepted on `minimumPassRatePercent`, where it unambiguously means a sub-1% floor the evaluato
r can act on, and REJECTED on the bare `minimumPassRate`, where `0.8` cannot be told apart from a fraction sent by mistake and wou
ld silently make the gate unfailable. Neither field ever reinterprets a value. A per-case `passThreshold` IS a fraction; this suit
"description": "A percent in [0, 100]. The whole range is usable, sub-1 values included \u2014 the unit is in the field
name, so nothing is ambiguous. Note that the GitHub Checks gate rounds the measured rate to an integer before comparing (to stay i
n step with the eval UI), so a floor below 0.5 behaves there as if it were 0.5; the platform's own verdict compares unrounded."
